scenarios.description: Mandatory use case — full system from scratch
scenarios.requirement: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.
scenarios.cli_command: python main.py --auto --requirement "Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics."

key_decisions: Cache-aside pattern: Redis hot-path, PostgreSQL durable store
Async analytics: fire-and-forget, never blocks redirect
Idempotency: duplicate URLs return same short code

scenarios.description: Add URL expiry feature to existing URL shortener
scenarios.requirement: Enhance the existing URL shortener to support configurable link expiration. URLs should automatically deactivate after a user-defined TTL.
scenarios.cli_command: python main.py --auto --requirement "Enhance the existing URL shortener to support configurable link expiration. URLs should automatically deactivate after a user-defined TTL." --codebase-path ./outputs

key_changes: Added expires_at column to urls table
Expiry check in UrlService.resolve() returns 410 Gone
Alembic migration script for expires_at column

scenarios.description: Vague performance requirement — system must detect and resolve ambiguities
scenarios.requirement: Make the service fast and scalable.
scenarios.cli_command: python main.py --auto --requirement "Make the service fast and scalable."

resolutions.scalable: Target: 10k RPS, horizontal scaling via stateless services + Redis cache
resolutions.fast: p99 redirect latency < 50ms via cache-first lookup

sample_output.normalized_requirement: [AMBIGUOUS] Make the service fast and scalable. — Normalized: Design and implement a production-ready system addressing the stated requirement with clear API contracts, persistence layer, test coverage, and operational documentation.
